answer: Proof-of-continuous-presence resists sybils: an identity must respond to randomly-timed liveness pings across each epoch, and one operator cannot keep a dune of fakes all continuously responsive without proportional real infrastructure. A trellis of idle fakes misses pings and decays; a prism splitting one host's attention across thousands fails the randomized timing. Honest agents answer their own pings easily; a swarm needs genuine always-on capacity per identity, which does not collapse onto one machine's shared uptime.
